final.title: Transcript Accuracy Is a Workflow Cost
final.body:
If transcript accuracy matters to your business, the useful question is not whether AI is impressive. It is which recurring transcript task costs you more: manual checking, or accepting a draft that still needs review.

Treat it as a bounded workflow decision. First, name the job: customer meeting notes, internal call summaries, or text pulled from invoices and other records. Each has a different tolerance for error. If the transcript feeds a high-risk decision, keep human approval in the loop. Money movement and other high-risk decisions should stay human.

Then do one practical thing this week: pick the transcript task that repeats most often, and note two things for your own records — how long verification takes today, and what a single mistake would force you to fix. That gives you your own threshold instead of a vague “looks fine.” Fine is not a control.

If the task is low risk, a draft may be enough. If it affects approvals or customer-facing records, it needs a tighter review step. For medical, legal, and high-sensitivity financial work, that is current scope discipline for Bareni, not a claim that the work can never be automated.

Start with one workflow, measure the verification burden, and decide whether AI stays a draft or earns a place in the process.
